# Awesome Phone Agents

[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/DU8866-nice/awesome-phone-agents?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/DU8866-nice/awesome-phone-agents) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/DU8866-nice/awesome-phone-agents?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/DU8866-nice/awesome-phone-agents/commits) [![License: CC0-1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-CC0--1.0-lightgrey?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen?style=flat-square)](CONTRIBUTING.md)

[简体中文](README.md) | **English**

> Open-source tools that let AI operate your phone: agent apps you install on the phone, Claude Code and Codex driving your phone, ADB phone-agent frameworks, and phone apps for steering coding agents on your computer. Each entry shows Android or iPhone support, whether it needs a computer or root, and whether it can use a local model. Stars refresh weekly.

The "AI phone" is moving from launch events into everyone's hands: say "sum up this group chat" or "compare prices and add it to my cart", and the AI opens the app, reads the screen, taps and types until the job is done. In the past few months the open-source community has produced a wave of these tools: apps you install on an Android phone, MCP servers that hand your phone to Claude Code or Codex, and open frameworks and models such as Zhipu's Open-AutoGLM and Alibaba's Mobile-Agent.

This list is for people who want to use them, not a paper list. It sorts the tools by your device and setup and shows, for each one, Android or iPhone support, whether it needs a computer or root, and whether it can use a local model.

61 projects · data refreshed 2026-11-23

<a id="rules"></a>
## Good to know

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - **Your screen goes to the model.** These tools "see" the phone through screenshots or the UI tree, so chats, one-time codes and balances may be in view. With a cloud model, that content goes to the model provider; tools marked 🔒 can use a local model so it stays on your devices.
> - **Confirm payments, transfers and deletions yourself.** Prefer tools that ask before paying or sending messages by default, and keep those confirmations on. Don't leave an agent unsupervised around wallets, banking or anything that can't be undone.
> - **Access granted is access used.** Accessibility, Shizuku, ADB and root all hand over most control of the phone. Download only from official repos, grant access only to tools you trust, and turn off remote access when you're done.
> - **Mind the platform rules.** Many apps forbid automation in their terms, and frequent automated taps can trip risk controls and get accounts restricted. Use these for your own chores, not to inflate numbers.
> - **iPhone limits.** iOS doesn't let ordinary apps control other apps, so most iPhone options need a computer, or a Mac to sign and install, with signing that needs upkeep.

This list does not include phone-farm, account-farming, fake-engagement or multi-account marketing tools, "stealth" cloud phones built to evade detection, or red-packet grabbers and game cheats.

**Legend**: 💻 Needs a computer (USB, ADB or same network) · 🔒 Can use a local model, screen stays on device · 🔑 Needs your own model key or account · 🔓 Needs root or jailbreak · 🀄 Chinese-friendly · 🆕 Created in the last 60 days · 💤 No update for over a year · 📦 Archived

> [!NOTE]
> Labels and supported systems come from each project's README and are only shown when the README says so; a missing label doesn't mean no. Listed means the README was checked, not that every tool was tested on a real phone.

<a id="cat-android"></a>
## Agent apps for Android phones

Install one APK and go, no computer needed. Most read and tap the screen through Accessibility; some use Shizuku or a virtual display so the agent works in the background without taking over your screen.

- **[dsh-Go](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go)** · ★ 30.5k · 🀄 🆕<br>A phone app for DeepSeek Harness with a built-in Linux environment: run it on the phone or switch to the DSH on your computer; it can read the screen and tap for you, with three confirmation levels and sensitive steps handed back by default.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · AGPL-3.0</sub><br><sub>💡 The iOS version is still in development with no public build</sub>
- **[Operit](https://github.com/AAswordman/Operit)** · ★ 9.8k · 🔒 🀄<br>An open-source agent platform for Android: it operates the phone UI, has a built-in browser and Ubuntu terminal, long-term memory, MCP and skills, and works with cloud models or local MNN and llama.cpp models.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · LGPL-3.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Operates the UI through Accessibility, Shizuku or root; more access unlocks more</sub>
- **[Mika](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika)** · ★ 9.7k · 🔑 🆕<br>Say what you need and it works your apps and the web on a hidden background screen until it's done, while you keep using your phone; it can sum up a group chat or add a pick to your cart and stop before checkout.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 There is no Mika server; use your own model key or sign in with ChatGPT, xAI or OpenRouter. Operating apps needs Android 12+</sub>
- **[andee](https://github.com/kuafuai/andee)** · ★ 6.2k · 🀄<br>An AI that lives on your phone or Mac and uses any app the way you do: no integrations, no root, no cable, any model, with long-term memory.<br><sub>Android / macOS · updated 2026-11</sub><br><sub>💡 The README's one-click install goes through a paid third-party build service; you can also download a release and set up your own model</sub>
- **[DSHA](https://github.com/DSH-APP/DSHA)** · ★ 3.7k · 🀄<br>An Android launcher that runs the full DeepSeek Harness on your phone with a built-in Ubuntu environment; no root or Termux, ready after install.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 Needs Android 11+ and arm64</sub>
- **[nanoMuse](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse)** · ★ 3.7k<br>An open-source personal agent with one name and look across phone, desktop and web that does things rather than just answering; the phone app, desktop app and relay are all in the repo and can be self-hosted.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · GPL-3.0</sub><br><sub>💡 The community relay has a free allowance, then you use your own key; the iPhone app is on TestFlight</sub>
- **[Eta](https://github.com/Mangi-11/Eta)** · ★ 3.1k · 🔑 🀄<br>A third-party system-level assistant: set it as the default digital assistant and long-press power to call it; it works across apps and handles calendar, alarms and notes, with deep integration for ColorOS and HyperOS.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · GPL-3.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Android 13+ on ARM64; core features need no root, while root and LSPosed unlock deeper access</sub>
- **[OmniBot](https://github.com/omnimind-ai/OmniBot)** · ★ 2.2k · 🀄<br>An on-device AI assistant that puts chat, agent tools, a local workspace and system integration in one app; with your permission and no root it manages calendar, contacts, reminders and files.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11</sub><br><sub>💡 The iOS and macOS version is a separate project, ViaVera</sub>
- **[PhoneGo](https://github.com/HKUDS/PhoneGo)** · ★ 1.5k<br>A phone agent from the HKUDS team that compiles common screens into a map ahead of time, so most steps are fast, repeatable commands; only unseen screens go to the vision model.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[opendroid](https://github.com/JMAN730/opendroid)** · ★ 1.3k · 🔒<br>An Android agent that plans multi-step tasks, executes and verifies each step, reads the screen through screenshots for vision models and supports importing local models.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11</sub>
- **[OneBox](https://github.com/wangzhishou/OneBox)** · ★ 1.2k · 🀄<br>OneBox, a free Android agent and toolbox: one sentence and the built-in agent drives 90+ in-app tools for images, PDFs, bookkeeping and files.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 The agent stays inside OneBox's own sandbox; it doesn't read contacts or SMS or operate other apps</sub>
- **[PalmClaw](https://github.com/ModalityDance/PalmClaw)** · ★ 1.2k · 🔑 🀄<br>An agent framework that runs natively on Android: sessions, memory, skills and tools live on the phone, device actions are checked against permissions and your confirmation, with scheduled tasks and MCP.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · AGPL-3.0</sub>
- **[PokeClaw](https://github.com/agents-io/PokeClaw)** · ★ 1.2k · 🔒<br>An open-source app that operates the phone with Gemma 4 running on the device; local mode needs no account or API key, and harder tasks can switch to a cloud model.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-06 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Android 9+; on CPU-only phones the model takes about 45 seconds to warm up</sub>
- **[DSH-Android](https://github.com/jackwener/DSH-Android)** · ★ 1.0k · 🔑 🀄 🆕 📦<br>One APK runs DeepSeek Harness on Android with no root or computer: send messages, sum up group chats, tidy files and change settings; with Shizuku or ADB it works on a virtual display and leaves your screen alone.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Sign in to DeepSeek or add an API key, or use another provider; arm64, Android 10+</sub>
- **[DSHBox](https://github.com/WSK-build/DSHBox)** · ★ 767 · 🀄<br>A mobile app for DeepSeek Harness that runs it locally on a phone or tablet or connects remotely, with a terminal, file manager, browser automation and phone control; no root or Termux.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · GPL-3.0</sub>
- **[Ruto-GLM](https://github.com/iamr0s/Ruto-GLM)** · ★ 734 · 🀄<br>A phone-side automation framework built on Open-AutoGLM: with Shizuku it runs tasks on a virtual display in the background, leaving your main screen free, and can run app instances side by side.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-01</sub><br><sub>💡 Needs Shizuku</sub>
- **[Agora](https://github.com/newo-ether/Agora)** · ★ 653 · 🔑<br>A bring-your-own-key LLM client for Android with multiple providers, agent workflows and remote device control.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · GPL-3.0</sub><br><sub>💡 The author warns a third party repackaged it under another name; download from the official repo</sub>
- **[zafiro](https://github.com/niki914/zafiro)** · ★ 392 · 🔑<br>An Android agent that understands the screen and works across apps, with skills, MCP, memory, Termux, a safety guard and session management.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 Uses Accessibility for native apps and Shizuku for others, no root needed</sub>

<a id="cat-iphone"></a>
## Agent apps for iPhone

iOS doesn't let ordinary apps control other apps, so few iPhone options can tap the screen for you, and most need a Mac to sign and install first. To drive an iPhone from an AI on your computer, see the next section.

- **[roubao](https://github.com/Turbo1123/roubao)** · ★ 2.4k · 💻 🀄<br>Roubao 2.0 lets AI operate your iPhone directly: read the screen, tap, type and finish tasks across apps; once set up it runs on the iPhone alone, with no jailbreak or extra hardware.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 First setup needs a Mac and cable to build and sign, and the signing needs upkeep; developer preview</sub>
- **[PhoneClaw](https://github.com/kellyvv/PhoneClaw)** · ★ 1.3k · 🔒<br>Turns your phone into a local agent runtime: runs Gemma 4 and MiniCPM-V on the iPhone and gets work done through Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, Clipboard and other native skills.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-08 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Available on TestFlight; needs iOS 17+</sub>
- **[PhoneAgent](https://github.com/rounak/PhoneAgent)** · ★ 808 · 🔑<br>An experiment with an in-app iPhone agent that works across iPhone apps, plus a bridge that lets Codex and other computer agents control an iPhone or Android phone.<br><sub>iPhone / Android · updated 2026-08 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 The in-app agent uses the OpenAI API with your own key</sub>

<a id="cat-remote"></a>
## Let Claude Code or Codex drive your phone

Connect your phone to your computer and hand it to the AI agent you already use through MCP: good for gathering information, repeating chores or letting AI test your own app.

- **[mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp)** · ★ 10.8k · 💻 🀄<br>A phone MCP server that lets AI agents drive real iOS and Android devices, simulators and emulators through accessibility snapshots or screenshot taps.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub>
- **[iPhone-use](https://github.com/zhongerxin/iPhone-use)** · ★ 5.1k · 💻 🀄 🆕<br>Lets Codex, WorkBuddy and others operate a real iPhone over USB: open apps, read pages, tap, scroll and type, with a live screen in the sidebar.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-10 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 Needs a Mac and WebDriverAgent signed onto the phone; sends anonymous usage stats by default, set IPHONE_USE_ANALYTICS=0 to turn off</sub>
- **[pinky](https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky)** · ★ 2.7k · 💻 🀄 🆕<br>Lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP agent use a real iPhone or Android phone: you watch on your computer, approve risky steps, take over any time and replay afterwards.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux; asks before payments by default</sub>
- **[android-remote-control-mcp](https://github.com/danielealbano/android-remote-control-mcp)** · ★ 861<br>An Android app that runs an MCP server on the phone, so Claude and other models can connect remotely to read the UI, tap, type and swipe; an optional privacy mode hides emails, card numbers and other personal data before it reaches the model.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11</sub>
- **[phoneuse](https://github.com/lxe/phoneuse)** · ★ 705 · 💻 🆕<br>See and operate an unmodified iPhone from your computer: AirPlay mirroring in, Bluetooth mouse and keyboard out, so Claude Code and Codex can tap and type with your permission; no jailbreak or cable.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 Alpha; builds for Linux and macOS 15+, Windows from source</sub>
- **[ios-mcp](https://github.com/witchan/ios-mcp)** · ★ 701 · 🔓 🀄<br>An MCP server for jailbroken iPhones: touch gestures, hardware buttons, text input, screenshots, app management and accessibility elements.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-09 · MIT</sub>
- **[iCTRL](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL)** · ★ 648 · 💻<br>An AI-friendly iOS automation service built on XCUITest that lets agents operate an iPhone or iPad.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 The author says it is for testing and research only; the pairing key means full control of the phone</sub>

<a id="cat-frameworks"></a>
## Phone agent frameworks: a computer drives the phone over ADB

These run on a computer and connect to the phone over ADB or WebDriverAgent, with a vision model reading the screen, planning and acting. Some command-line comfort helps; they suit long-running or scheduled tasks.

- **[Open-AutoGLM](https://github.com/zai-org/Open-AutoGLM)** · ★ 26.7k · 💻 🀄<br>Zhipu's open phone agent model and framework: say "search for food on Xiaohongshu" and it reads the screen, plans and finishes the job, with confirmation for sensitive steps, hand-over for logins and CAPTCHAs, and remote ADB over Wi-Fi.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-03 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Host the model yourself or use a third-party model service</sub>
- **[artemis](https://github.com/google/artemis)** · ★ 17.9k · 💻<br>From Google: turns natural-language instructions into reliable Android automation across apps, for test flows and everyday tasks, and exposes MCP for Claude Code and other agents.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-10 · Apache-2.0</sub>
- **[mobilerun](https://github.com/droidrun/mobilerun)** · ★ 10.1k · 💻 🔒<br>An open-source framework for operating Android and iOS devices with natural language, also used for app testing, with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama and other models.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 A paid cloud service exists but isn't needed to run locally</sub>
- **[MobileAgent](https://github.com/X-PLUG/MobileAgent)** · ★ 9.4k · 💻 🀄<br>The Mobile-Agent family from Alibaba's Tongyi Lab: a phone GUI agent framework and the GUI-Owl models, with online demos or local deployment.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[AppAgent](https://github.com/TencentQQGYLab/AppAgent)** · ★ 6.9k · 💻 💤<br>Tencent's multimodal phone agent that learns a new app by exploring on its own or watching a human demo, then taps and swipes like a person.<br><sub>Android · updated 2025-03 · MIT</sub>
- **[mobile-use](https://github.com/minitap-ai/mobile-use)** · ★ 3.4k · 💻 🔑<br>An open-source agent that controls Android or iOS devices in plain language, from sending messages to navigating complex apps, with OpenAI, Google, xAI, OpenRouter and other models.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub>
- **[MobiAgent](https://github.com/IPADS-SAI/MobiAgent)** · ★ 1.9k · 🀄<br>A customizable mobile agent system from the IPADS team with the MobiMind models, the AgentRR acceleration framework, the MobiFlow benchmark and an Android app.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-07 · Apache-2.0</sub>
- **[AutoCua](https://github.com/ComputerUseAgent/AutoCua)** · ★ 1.3k · 💻 🆕<br>A team of AI agents that works your Mac, Windows, Linux, phone and browser.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[AutoGLM-GUI](https://github.com/suyiiyii/AutoGLM-GUI)** · ★ 1.1k · 💻 🀄<br>A graphical interface for AutoGLM: connect phones and give tasks in the browser, with scheduled runs, Docker deployment, history and multiple devices.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub>

<a id="cat-coding"></a>
## Steer Claude Code and Codex from your phone

The coding agent runs on your computer while your phone shows progress, approves the next step and sends new tasks, so work continues when you step away.

- **[t3code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)** · ★ 73.4k<br>An open-source control plane for coding agents: they run on your machine with your own subscriptions, so you start a thread at your desk and approve the next step from your phone; works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[paseo](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo)** · ★ 24.7k<br>One interface for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and OpenCode: agents run in parallel on your machine, you move work forward from phone, desktop or web, with voice mode and no telemetry.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11</sub>
- **[claudecodeui](https://github.com/siteboon/claudecodeui)** · ★ 14.7k<br>A desktop and mobile web UI for Claude Code, Cursor CLI and Codex, usable locally or remotely and self-hosted with one npx command.<br><sub>Web · updated 2026-11 · AGPL-3.0</sub>
- **[coucou](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou)** · ★ 7.4k · 🆕<br>A tiny friend in your Mac's notch that watches your coding agent sessions and follows you to iPhone or Android, with approvals on the Lock Screen, Dynamic Island and widgets.<br><sub>iPhone / Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[nexting](https://github.com/Nexting-ai/nexting)** · ★ 2.4k<br>Remote control for your own agents: connect from your phone to Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Cursor on a Mac or Windows PC to view sessions and send tasks.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[happier](https://github.com/happier-dev/happier)** · ★ 2.3k · 🀄<br>A multi-device control center for orchestrating Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents from phone, desktop and browser; open source, self-hostable and end-to-end encrypted.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[collie](https://github.com/AltanS/collie)** · ★ 1.7k<br>An open-source phone web app that shows your terminal agents, including Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, and lets you answer them remotely; you host it on your own computer alongside Herdr.<br><sub>Web · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[ccpocket](https://github.com/K9i-0/ccpocket)** · ★ 1.1k · 🀄<br>Coding agents in your pocket: chat with Codex and Claude from your phone to send instructions, approve steps and see results, then continue on a tablet or Mac.<br><sub>Android / iPhone · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[Mobile-Harness](https://github.com/techjarves/Mobile-Harness)** · ★ 982<br>An AI development workspace on Android: chat with coding agents, edit projects, run real Linux commands and preview web servers on the phone.<br><sub>Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[codex-relay](https://github.com/gronxb/codex-relay)** · ★ 755<br>A phone companion for the Codex CLI: a local relay in your workspace pairs over your own network so you can follow or steer Codex sessions from the phone while code and state stay on your computer.<br><sub>iPhone · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub>

<a id="faq"></a>
## FAQ

**How is this different from the AI assistant my phone maker ships?**
Built-in assistants have system-level access and feel smoother, but only on certain phones and with a fixed model. The open-source tools here install on most Android phones, let you pick the model and let you read the code; the trade-off is setup work and reliability that varies by app.

**Do I need root?**
Mostly no. Android apps usually use Accessibility; working on a background virtual display usually needs Shizuku or wireless debugging. Only a few tools need root, and jailbreak-based iPhone tools are marked 🔓.

**Does it cost anything?**
The tools are open source. Cloud models cost whatever the provider charges; tools such as PokeClaw and PhoneClaw can run a local model on the phone for free, but need capable hardware and are slower.

**What is it best at?**
Jobs with lots of reading and tapping but little judgment: summing up chats and posts, looking things up, comparing prices, filling forms, tidying files and testing your own app. For anything involving money or privacy, let it prepare and tap the last step yourself.

**How often are stars updated?**
Every Monday GitHub Actions refreshes the stars and re-sorts the list, and links are checked weekly.

<a id="finder"></a>
## Let your AI agent pick

This list is also a skill. Install the [`skills/phone-agent-finder`](skills/phone-agent-finder) folder in your AI agent (or run `npx skills add DU8866-nice/awesome-phone-agents`) and ask:

> I have a Pixel, don't want to root it or plug it into a computer, and want AI to sum up a few group chats every day. Which tool should I use?

It picks two or three entries for your phone, whether you have a computer, your privacy needs and the task, explains why, and points out what to watch for with payments and privacy.
